newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia quarterly mineral export earnings fall.
newsitem.headline: Australia quarterly mineral export earnings fall.

text.p: Export earnings by Australia's minerals and energy sector declined 1.3 percent to A$8.41 billion in the quarter ended March 31, with gold, crude oil and most nonferrous metals showing falls, the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) said.

"This weaker perfomance reflected reduced export earnings across a range of commodities, with gold, crude oil, copper, lead, diamonds and some mineral sands being among the more notable," ABARE said in its latest issue of Australian Mineral Statistics journal released on Wednesday.

The index of export prices of Australian mineral resources increased by 1.7 percent in the March quarter compared with the previous quarter, with the energy minerals component increasing by 3.4 percent and the metals and other minerals component rising 0.5 percent, ABARE said.
Export earnings from refined gold fell five percent to A$1.176 billion, while crude oil and other refinery feedstock fell eight percent to A$489 million, the government forecasting agency said.
Earnings from copper exports declined 16.5 percent to A$227 million, lead was down 30 percent to A$94 million and zircon fell 41 percent to A$40 million, ABARE said.
Diamond export earnings fell 17 percent to A$118 million, it said.
Other commodities showing declines in the March quarter included alumina, gems, liquified petroleum gas, refinery petroleum products, tin, ilmenite and natural rutile, ABARE said.
Refined aluminium export earnings rose 28 percent to A$546 million, nickel was up 19 percent to A$306 million and liquified natural gas rose 12 percent to A$428 million, ABARE figures showed.
Iron ore export earnings grew five precent to A$782 million in the quarter, while a five precent rise in zinc exports took earnings to A$201 million, ABARE said.
"In the majority of cases, increased export prices were the main influnece on these increases in earnings," ABARE said.
Smaller increases were recorded for steaming and coking coal, magnesite, refined silver, uranium and titanium pigment, ABARE said.
